newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Kwong Sang off after privatisation fails.
newsitem.headline: Kwong Sang off after privatisation fails.

text.p: Kwong Sang Hong International Ltd shares fell on Thursday after an attempt by controlling parent Peregrine Investments Holdings Ltd to privatise the property company failed, brokers said on Thursday.
Kwong Sang Hong shares fell HK$0.725, or 16.76 percent, to HK$3.60 in mid-morning trade on volume of 12.59 million shares.
Investors who bought the shares due to the high privatisation offer of HK$4.37 per share, were cutting their losses, brokers said.
Peregrine, which owns 51.9 percent of Kwong Sang Hong, said on Wednesday the number of shareholders who voted in favour of the privatisation proposal was below the requisite majority.
"Apart from the sale of shares by short term investors, I think it has a neutral impact on the fundametals of both companies," said Sean Li, Amsteel Securities associate director.

"Expectations of strong earnings growth at Peregrine, due to an active stock market, should give the shares a boost in the near run," he added. Shares of Peregrine rose HK$0.10 to HK$13.95 in late morning trade. Volume was 2.34 million shares.
